verdicts.note: AJHE 2023. Mandate GENEROSITY (a continuous access margin) against multiple births. Best-identified record so far on the A.12 side of the boundary; both chapters should see it.
No abstract; title decisive on outcome.
Qualitative, permanent childlessness after delay. Belief side.
No abstract. 'Outcomes' after comprehensive mandates — could be per-cycle, multiples or births.
IVF subsidy against ADOPTION rates. Off-estimand but conceptually sharp: it is a direct test of what ART substitutes for, which is the counterfactual arm 1 assumes away.
Paratext record titled 'References'. An indexing artifact, not a work.
UK survey, elective OC for age-related fertility decline. Elective indication named explicitly; outcome is awareness, not births.
Stochastic projections of future US ART live births.
Why people postpone — A.15's question directly.
Country-level delay/fertility relationship; no ART channel.
Editorial contesting the mandate-to-transfer-practice link. No abstract.
Public opinion about IVF coverage, not an effect of coverage.

German panel: self-perceived infertility is NOT always associated with fewer children. Off-cell but it tests A.17's own premise — that impaired fecundity binds realized fertility. Flag for the chapter's framing section.
Preprint version of the Prag & Mills 2017 anchor. Version-of-record duplicate — flag.
A coding of state infertility-insurance law. This is the EXPOSURE INSTRUMENT arm 2 depends on: mandate 'generosity' is not binary and how it is coded drives every estimate in the cell.
Singapore, 2026. Fertility knowledge and attitudes toward preservation among educated youth.
Canadian childless adults' willingness to use assisted reproduction. Belief side.
Education/occupation and childlessness; no ART channel.
Cohort fertility decline by education, Australia.
IFFS consensus on declining fertility and family building. Likely touches ART's role but is a position document, not an estimate.
Men's fertility knowledge and behaviour, review. Belief side; notable for covering men, who are absent from most of this cell.
Overview chapter on MAR in developed countries; whether it quantifies a share is not visible.
IVF money-back guarantees and service quality. A price/market-design mechanism with a selection outcome — relevant to how the access margin actually operates, not to births.
Thesis on intergenerational transmission of fertility timing. A.19's.
NULL FINDING: mandates NOT associated with improved racial/ethnic disparities in utilisation. Included on the same terms as a positive result.

AER 2018 — the most rigorous access-margin record found so far. Structural treatment of out-of-pocket price, patient entry, and the incentive to transfer more embryos. Note the endogenous-multiples channel it identifies: it is the mechanism A.12 owns, arising inside an A.17 exposure.
No abstract; title decisive. Recession interacted with mandates — an income-by-access margin.
The intention-realization gap across 20 countries. Off-cell, but it is the quantity ART is claimed to close, so it bounds what a recovery arm could possibly deliver.
Preprint of the education/occupation childlessness paper above.
Women's employment life cycle. C.2.e's.
Swedish academics' fertility awareness and intentions. Same research group as the Lampic 2006 anchor.
Systematic review of fertility awareness. The best summary of the BELIEF side; useful precisely for showing how much of P6 is belief and how little is behaviour.
1989 review of natural fertility and fecundity.
Psychosocial determinants of delay; ART is not the exposure.
Encyclopedia entry on below-replacement fertility.
Late parenthood in East Asia.
Finnish students' childbearing desires.

UK vs Australia embryo-transfer policy, outcome is the ART multiple-birth rate. NOTE for A.12: it attributes Australia's success to supportive PUBLIC FUNDING — an A.17 exposure producing an A.12 outcome, which is the boundary case in its purest form.
Ecological correlation of TFR, ART utilisation and GDP across Europe using ESHRE EIM cycles. Weak design, on-estimand.
Proposal for fertility assessment and counselling — an intervention on the belief side.
Regional diffusion of late fertility in Europe.
Titled exactly on A.17's estimand — 'The Demographic Consequences of Assisted Reproductive Technologies'. Preprint; whether it counts or estimates is not visible.
Van de Kaa's SDT statement, 1987. D.1.a's.
Econometric methods paper on contaminated instruments, reached through a citation path.
No abstract. Access disparities WITHIN a mandate state — speaks to whether the mandate binds.
Against using the period TFR. Off-cell but directly relevant to PI call 4: whether ART's contribution is expressed against period or cohort fertility changes the number.
PM2.5 and fertility rates. B.2/B.6's.

J. Population Economics: ART AFFORDABILITY against women's MARRIAGE timing. Identified on an A.17 exposure with a union outcome — the mirror of the divorce paper in batch 1. Off-estimand for demographic significance, on-mechanism for how access changes behaviour.
Review of IVF cost-effectiveness studies.
Italian Jobs Act and fertility. C.5's (employment insecurity), well identified but not an ART exposure.
Race/ethnicity and education in completed fertility.
Attitudes to MAR under Hungarian pronatalism. Politics of access, not its effect.
Ukraine: ~1.6% of births ART-conceived. Non-OECD-core; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8 at extraction.
Goldstein et al. on the reversal of lowest-low fertility.
Cohort fertility forecasts for 37 countries.
Postponement and childlessness in British cohorts.

**A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL** providing information on age-related fertility decline and measuring family/career expectations. The strongest design found in P6 by a wide margin — but the outcome is still an EXPECTATION, not a behaviour. If nothing better appears, the chapter's P6 verdict is that the belief link is experimentally established and the behaviour link is not.
Dutch microsimulation of the fertility gap; likely the companion to the 2026 Human Reproduction microsimulation in batch 1.
BMJ 1991 age-fecundity curve. Not an A.17 estimate; it supplies the biological parameters every recovery simulation in P4 runs on, so it belongs in the chain of evidence rather than in the cell.
Intentions to use preservation against age-related decline. Elective indication; belief outcome. The elective cell continues to fill with attitude studies rather than birth outcomes.
